source.text: הוֹד֣וּ לַ֭יהוָה קִרְא֣וּ בִּשְׁמ֑וֹ הוֹדִ֥יעוּ בָ֝עַמִּ֗ים עֲלִילוֹתָֽיו׃

records.literal_gloss: Give thanks to YHWH; call on his name; make known among the peoples his deeds.

en.L: Give thanks to {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}; call on {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} name; make known among the peoples {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} deeds.
en.B: Thank {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} and call on {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} name; tell every people what {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} has done.
en.R: Thank {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}! Pray to {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} by name. Tell people everywhere what {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} has done.

fr.L: Rendez grâce {{divine_name:au SEIGNEUR|à Yahvé}} ; invoquez {{deity_pronoun:son|Son}} nom ; faites connaître parmi les peuples {{deity_pronoun:ses|Ses}} hauts faits.
fr.B: Rendez grâce {{divine_name:au SEIGNEUR|à Yahvé}} et invoquez {{deity_pronoun:son|Son}} nom ; racontez à tous les peuples ce qu’{{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} a fait.
fr.R: Remerciez {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} ! Priez-{{deity_pronoun:le|Le}} en l’appelant par {{deity_pronoun:son|Son}} nom. Dites aux gens du monde entier ce qu’{{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} a fait.

sw.L: Mshukuruni {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}}; liitieni jina {{deity_pronoun:lake|Lake}}; julisheni kati ya mataifa matendo {{deity_pronoun:yake|Yake}}.
sw.B: Mshukuruni {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}}, liitieni jina {{deity_pronoun:lake|Lake}}; waambieni mataifa yote aliyoyatenda.
sw.R: Mshukuruni {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}}! Mwombeni kwa jina {{deity_pronoun:lake|Lake}}. Waambieni watu kila mahali aliyoyatenda.

decisions.reason: Verses 1-15 appear, with small differences, in 1 Chronicles 16:8-22, in the song sung when David brought the ark of God to Jerusalem. The song there goes on with Psalm 96 and with lines from Psalm 106 (1 Chronicles 16:23-36).

decisions.choice: a psalm with no title that retells history
decisions.reason: The Hebrew gives this psalm no title. It retells God's faithfulness from Abraham to the gift of the land; Psalm 106, its partner, retells the same years as a story of Israel's unfaithfulness. Together they close Book Four of the Psalms.

decisions.choice: call on his name: pray to him, or proclaim him
decisions.reason: To call on (or "in") the name of the LORD is to pray to him by name, as Abraham did (Genesis 12:8); it can also mean to proclaim his name aloud. The next line, "make known", leans toward praise spoken before others.
Readable says what calling on the name means (m3).

decisions.choice: "le SEIGNEUR" in capitals for the divine name, with "Yahvé" as the reader's alternative, for Psalms 105–118
decisions.reason: As in the Pentateuch and Proverbs: the capitals mark the name, as the English "the LORD" does. "L'Éternel", the Segond tradition, is the form a reviewer may prefer.

decisions.choice: "rendre grâce" (Literal, Balanced), "remercier" (Readable) for hodu; "louer" for hallel and "bénir" for barak, for Psalms 105–118
decisions.reason: The three verbs of praise keep three French words so that a reader can follow them through the psalms. Readable uses the everyday verb, as the English Readable says "Thank".

decisions.choice: deity_pronoun spans only on free pronouns such as "jina lake" and "matendo yake"
alternatives: a span on every pronoun for God, as in English
decisions.reason: Swahili marks most pronouns inside the verb ("aliyoyatenda", "mwombeni"), and a verb prefix cannot take a capital, so these psalms have fewer deity_pronoun spans than the English. Only the separate words (possessives like "lake", "yake", "wake", and "yeye", "naye") change with the setting.

source.text: שִֽׁירוּ־ל֭וֹזַמְּרוּ־ל֑וֹ שִׂ֝֗יחוּ בְּכָל־נִפְלְאוֹתָֽיו׃

records.literal_gloss: Sing to him, make music to him; tell of all his wonders.

en.L: Sing to {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}, make music to {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}; tell of all {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} wonders.
en.B: Sing to {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}, play and sing {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} praise; talk of all the wonderful things {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} has done.
en.R: Sing to {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}! Make music for {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}! Talk about all the amazing things {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} has done.

fr.L: Chantez-{{deity_pronoun:lui|Lui}}, jouez pour {{deity_pronoun:lui|Lui}} ; parlez de toutes {{deity_pronoun:ses|Ses}} merveilles.
fr.B: Chantez pour {{deity_pronoun:lui|Lui}}, chantez {{deity_pronoun:sa|Sa}} louange avec des instruments ; parlez de toutes les merveilles qu’{{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} a faites.
fr.R: Chantez pour {{deity_pronoun:lui|Lui}} ! Jouez de la musique pour {{deity_pronoun:lui|Lui}} ! Parlez de toutes les choses étonnantes qu’{{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} a faites.

sw.L: Mwimbieni, mpigieni muziki; simulieni maajabu {{deity_pronoun:yake|Yake}} yote.
sw.B: Mwimbieni, pigeni vinanda mkimsifu; zungumzeni mambo yote ya ajabu aliyoyatenda.
sw.R: Mwimbieni! Mpigieni muziki! Zungumzeni juu ya mambo yote ya ajabu aliyoyafanya.

decisions.reason: The verb (zimmer) is used of songs sung to the music of instruments.

decisions.choice: tell of: talk about, think over
decisions.reason: The verb (siach) is to go over something in the mind and in speech; here it is telling others.
The word (nifla'ot) is used of the great acts of God at the exodus (Exodus 3:20), which the psalm goes on to tell.

source.text: הִֽ֭תְהַלְלוּ בְּשֵׁ֣ם קָדְשׁ֑וֹ יִ֝שְׂמַ֗ח לֵ֤ב׀מְבַקְשֵׁ֬י יְהוָֽה׃

records.literal_gloss: Boast in [the] name of his holiness; let it rejoice, [the] heart of those who seek YHWH.

en.L: Glory in {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} holy name; let the heart of those who seek {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} rejoice.
en.B: Take pride in {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} holy name; let all who look to {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} be glad at heart.
en.R: Be proud of {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} holy name. Everyone who looks for {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} should be glad.

fr.L: Glorifiez-vous de {{deity_pronoun:son|Son}} saint nom ; que se réjouisse le cœur de ceux qui cherchent {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}}.
fr.B: Soyez fiers de {{deity_pronoun:son|Son}} saint nom ; que tous ceux qui se tournent vers {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} aient le cœur dans la joie.
fr.R: Soyez fiers de {{deity_pronoun:son|Son}} saint nom. Que tous ceux qui cherchent {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} soient joyeux.

sw.L: Jisifuni katika jina {{deity_pronoun:lake|Lake}} takatifu; moyo wa wale wamtafutao {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} ufurahi.
sw.B: Oneni fahari katika jina {{deity_pronoun:lake|Lake}} takatifu; wote wanaomtafuta {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} wafurahi mioyoni mwao.
sw.R: Jivunieni jina {{deity_pronoun:lake|Lake}} takatifu. Kila anayemtafuta {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} na afurahi.

decisions.reason: The verb (hithallel) is to boast. Here the boast is not in oneself but in the LORD (34:3; Jeremiah 9:23).

decisions.choice: the name of his holiness: his holy name
decisions.reason: Hebrew often uses a noun ("of holiness") where other languages use an adjective; the name stands for God himself as he has made himself known.

decisions.choice: seek: turn to in prayer and worship
decisions.reason: To seek the LORD (biqqesh) is to come to him for help and to worship him, often at his sanctuary (24:6; 27:8).

source.text: דִּרְשׁ֣וּ יְהוָ֣ה וְעֻזּ֑וֹ בַּקְּשׁ֖וּ פָנָ֣יו תָּמִֽיד׃

records.literal_gloss: Seek YHWH and his strength; seek his face continually.

en.L: Seek {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} and {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} strength; seek {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} face continually.
en.B: Turn to {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} and to {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} strength; come into {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} presence again and again.
en.R: Turn to {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} and depend on {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} strength. Never stop coming to worship {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}.

fr.L: Recherchez {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} et {{deity_pronoun:sa|Sa}} force ; cherchez {{deity_pronoun:sa|Sa}} face continuellement.
fr.B: Tournez-vous vers {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} et vers {{deity_pronoun:sa|Sa}} force ; venez en {{deity_pronoun:sa|Sa}} présence sans cesse.
fr.R: Tournez-vous vers {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} et comptez sur {{deity_pronoun:sa|Sa}} force. Ne cessez jamais de venir {{deity_pronoun:l’|L’}}adorer.

sw.L: Mtafuteni {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} na nguvu {{deity_pronoun:zake|Zake}}; utafuteni uso {{deity_pronoun:wake|Wake}} daima.
sw.B: Mgeukieni {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} na nguvu {{deity_pronoun:zake|Zake}}; njooni mbele {{deity_pronoun:zake|Zake}} tena na tena.
sw.R: Mgeukieni {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} na mtegemee nguvu {{deity_pronoun:zake|Zake}}. Msiache kamwe kuja kumwabudu.

decisions.choice: seek: two verbs with the same sense
decisions.reason: The first verb (darash) is to inquire of or turn to; the second (biqqesh) is the verb of verse 3. Both mean coming to the LORD.

decisions.choice: his strength: the strength he gives, or the ark
alternatives: the ark, the sign of his strength
decisions.reason: The phrase can mean the strength that comes from God. In 78:61 and 132:8 "his strength" is a name for the ark, which fits the setting in 1 Chronicles 16, where the ark is brought to Jerusalem.

decisions.choice: seek his face: come before him
decisions.reason: God's face is his presence; to seek it is to come before him in worship (24:6; 27:8).

decisions.choice: come into his presence again and again (B); Never stop coming to worship him (R)
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable say what seeking his face means (m3).

source.text: זִכְר֗וּ נִפְלְאוֹתָ֥יו אֲשֶׁר־עָשָׂ֑ה מֹ֝פְתָ֗יו וּמִשְׁפְּטֵי־פִֽיו׃

records.literal_gloss: Remember his wonders which he has done, his signs and [the] judgments of his mouth,

en.L: Remember {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} wonders that {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} has done, {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} signs and the judgments of {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} mouth,
en.B: Call to mind the wonders {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} has worked, {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} signs, and the verdicts {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} spoke,
en.R: Remember the amazing things {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} has done. Remember {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} miracles and the judgments {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} announced.

fr.L: Souvenez-vous de {{deity_pronoun:ses|Ses}} merveilles qu’{{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} a faites, de {{deity_pronoun:ses|Ses}} signes et des jugements de {{deity_pronoun:sa|Sa}} bouche,
fr.B: Rappelez-vous les merveilles qu’{{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} a accomplies, {{deity_pronoun:ses|Ses}} signes et les sentences qu’{{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} a prononcées,
fr.R: Souvenez-vous des choses étonnantes qu’{{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} a faites. Souvenez-vous de {{deity_pronoun:ses|Ses}} miracles et des jugements qu’{{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} a annoncés.

sw.L: Kumbukeni maajabu {{deity_pronoun:yake|Yake}} aliyoyatenda, ishara {{deity_pronoun:zake|Zake}} na hukumu za kinywa {{deity_pronoun:chake|Chake}},
sw.B: Yakumbukeni maajabu aliyoyafanya, ishara {{deity_pronoun:zake|Zake}}, na hukumu alizozitamka,
sw.R: Kumbukeni mambo ya ajabu aliyoyafanya. Kumbukeni miujiza {{deity_pronoun:yake|Yake}} na hukumu alizozitangaza.

decisions.choice: signs: acts that point to God's power
decisions.reason: The word (mofet) is a sign or portent, used of the plagues on Egypt (Exodus 7:3; 11:9).

decisions.choice: the judgments of his mouth: the sentences he pronounced
decisions.reason: God spoke his judgments and they were carried out. The setting is the exodus, when he promised to bring Israel out "with great judgments" on Egypt (Exodus 6:6; 7:4).
Verse 6 names those who are called to remember, so the verse ends with a comma at Literal and Balanced.

source.text: זֶ֭רַע אַבְרָהָ֣ם עַבְדּ֑וֹ בְּנֵ֖י יַעֲקֹ֣ב בְּחִירָֽיו׃

records.literal_gloss: offspring of Abraham his servant, sons of Jacob, his chosen ones.

en.L: you offspring of Abraham {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} servant, you sons of Jacob, {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} chosen ones.
en.B: you descendants of {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} servant Abraham, you children of Jacob, the ones {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} chose.
en.R: Do this, you who come from Abraham, {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} servant, you descendants of Jacob, whom {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} chose.

fr.L: vous, descendance d’Abraham, {{deity_pronoun:son|Son}} serviteur, vous, fils de Jacob, {{deity_pronoun:ses|Ses}} élus.
fr.B: vous, descendants d’Abraham, {{deity_pronoun:son|Son}} serviteur, vous, enfants de Jacob, qu’{{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} a choisis.
fr.R: Faites-le, vous qui descendez d’Abraham, {{deity_pronoun:son|Son}} serviteur, vous, descendants de Jacob, qu’{{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} a choisis.

sw.L: ninyi uzao wa Abrahamu, mtumishi {{deity_pronoun:wake|Wake}}, ninyi wana wa Yakobo, wateule {{deity_pronoun:wake|Wake}}.
sw.B: ninyi wazao wa mtumishi {{deity_pronoun:wake|Wake}} Abrahamu, ninyi watoto wa Yakobo, aliowachagua.
sw.R: Fanyeni hivyo, ninyi mlio wa uzao wa Abrahamu, mtumishi {{deity_pronoun:wake|Wake}}, ninyi wazao wa Yakobo, aliowachagua.

decisions.choice: his servant: Abraham; his chosen ones: Jacob's children
alternatives: his servant: the people, as offspring of Abraham
decisions.reason: "His servant" stands beside Abraham, and "his chosen ones" (plural) beside the sons of Jacob. The people of Israel are addressed through their ancestors.
The parallel in 1 Chronicles 16:13 reads "offspring of Israel his servant" in place of Abraham.
"Sons of Jacob" means the whole people descended from him, so Balanced and Readable say "children"; Literal keeps "sons".
Readable ended verse 5 with a full stop, so it links the people addressed here to the commands before them.

decisions.choice: ʿeved is "esclave" at Literal and "serviteur" at Balanced and Readable for God's servants in general, in Psalms 105–118; "serviteur" at every level for a named servant of God (Abraham, Moses, David) and for "ton serviteur", the psalmist's name for himself; "esclave" at every level where slavery itself is meant (Joseph sold, 105:17)
decisions.reason: The Hebrew word covers both a slave and a king's or God's servant. Literal keeps the hard word, as the English Literal and the French Pentateuch do; Balanced and Readable say "serviteur", the honoured title of Abraham and Moses.

decisions.choice: ʿeved as "mtumishi" (servant) at every level; "mtumwa" (slave) only where slavery itself is meant (105:17)
decisions.reason: The Hebrew word covers both a slave and a king's or God's trusted servant. In the Psalms Swahili says "mtumishi" for ʿeved at every level, Literal included, for God's servants and the psalmist's name for himself; "mtumwa" is kept for slavery itself (Joseph sold, 105:17; the slaves of 123:2).

source.text: ה֭וּא יְהוָ֣ה אֱלֹהֵ֑ינוּ בְּכָל־הָ֝אָ֗רֶץ מִשְׁפָּטָֽיו׃

records.literal_gloss: He [is] YHWH our God; in all the earth [are] his judgments.

en.L: He [is] {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} our God; in all the earth [are] {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} judgments.
en.B: He, {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, is our God; {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} rulings reach the whole earth.
en.R: He is {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, our God. He judges what happens everywhere on earth.

fr.L: Lui, [il est] {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} notre Dieu ; dans toute la terre [sont] {{deity_pronoun:ses|Ses}} jugements.
fr.B: C’est {{deity_pronoun:lui|Lui}}, {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}}, qui est notre Dieu ; {{deity_pronoun:ses|Ses}} décisions s’étendent à toute la terre.
fr.R: Il est {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}}, notre Dieu. Il juge tout ce qui se passe sur la terre entière.

sw.L: Yeye [ni] {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} Mungu wetu; katika dunia yote [zipo] hukumu {{deity_pronoun:zake|Zake}}.
sw.B: Yeye, {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}}, ndiye Mungu wetu; maamuzi {{deity_pronoun:yake|Yake}} yanaifikia dunia yote.
sw.R: Yeye ni {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}}, Mungu wetu. Anahukumu yanayotokea kila mahali duniani.

decisions.reason: The pronoun stands first for emphasis: this God who did all these things is the LORD, Israel's own God.

decisions.choice: his judgments in all the earth
decisions.reason: The God of one people is judge of every nation; his rulings came on Egypt and on kings (verses 14, 27-36).

source.text: זָכַ֣ר לְעוֹלָ֣ם בְּרִית֑וֹ דָּבָ֥ר צִ֝וָּ֗ה לְאֶ֣לֶף דּֽוֹר׃

records.literal_gloss: He remembers forever his covenant, [the] word he commanded for a thousand generation[s],

en.L: He remembers {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} covenant forever, the word {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} commanded for a thousand generations,
en.B: He keeps {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} covenant in mind forever, the promise {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} laid down for a thousand generations,
en.R: He never forgets {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} covenant, the promise {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} made to last for a thousand generations.

fr.L: Il se souvient pour toujours de {{deity_pronoun:son|Son}} alliance, de la parole qu’{{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} a prescrite pour mille générations,
fr.B: Il garde {{deity_pronoun:son|Son}} alliance en mémoire pour toujours, la promesse qu’{{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} a établie pour mille générations,
fr.R: Il n’oublie jamais {{deity_pronoun:son|Son}} alliance, la promesse qu’{{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} a faite pour qu’elle dure mille générations.

sw.L: Analikumbuka agano {{deity_pronoun:lake|Lake}} milele, neno aliloliamuru kwa vizazi elfu,
sw.B: Analiweka agano {{deity_pronoun:lake|Lake}} moyoni milele, ahadi aliyoiweka kwa vizazi elfu,
sw.R: Kamwe hasahau agano {{deity_pronoun:lake|Lake}}, ahadi aliyoifanya idumu kwa vizazi elfu.

decisions.choice: remembers: keeps in mind and acts on it
decisions.reason: When God remembers his covenant he acts to keep it (Exodus 2:24; 6:5). The verb returns in verse 42, so the whole story is framed by God's remembering.
The parallel in 1 Chronicles 16:15 reads "Remember his covenant forever", a command to the people; here it is God who remembers.

decisions.choice: the word he commanded for a thousand generations: a promise without end
decisions.reason: The "word" is the promise of the covenant, set in place by God's command. "A thousand generations" means for all time (Deuteronomy 7:9).
Balanced and Readable say what the word is (m3).

source.text: אֲשֶׁ֣ר כָּ֭רַת אֶת־אַבְרָהָ֑ם וּשְׁב֖וּעָת֣וֹ לְיִשְׂחָֽק׃

records.literal_gloss: which he cut with Abraham, and his oath to Isaac,

en.L: which {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} cut with Abraham, and {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} oath to Isaac,
en.B: the covenant {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} made with Abraham, the oath {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} swore to Isaac,
en.R: He made it with Abraham, and {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} promised it to Isaac with an oath.

fr.L: qu’{{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} a tranchée avec Abraham, et {{deity_pronoun:son|Son}} serment à Isaac,
fr.B: l’alliance qu’{{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} a conclue avec Abraham, le serment qu’{{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} a fait à Isaac,
fr.R: Il l’a conclue avec Abraham, et {{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} l’a promise à Isaac par un serment.

sw.L: ambalo alilikata pamoja na Abrahamu, na kiapo {{deity_pronoun:chake|Chake}} kwa Isaka,
sw.B: agano alilofanya na Abrahamu, kiapo alichomwapia Isaka,
sw.R: Alilifanya na Abrahamu, na akamwahidi Isaka kwa kiapo.

decisions.choice: cut a covenant: make a covenant
decisions.reason: A covenant was "cut", perhaps from the animals cut in two when it was made, as in Genesis 15:9-18.

decisions.choice: the covenant with Abraham and the oath to Isaac
decisions.reason: God made his covenant with Abraham and promised him the land (Genesis 15:18; 17:7-8), swore by himself to bless him (Genesis 22:16-18), and confirmed the oath to Isaac (Genesis 26:3-4).

source.text: וַיַּֽעֲמִידֶ֣הָ לְיַעֲקֹ֣ב לְחֹ֑ק לְ֝יִשְׂרָאֵ֗ל בְּרִ֣ית עוֹלָֽם׃

records.literal_gloss: and he made it stand for Jacob as a statute, for Israel [as] an everlasting covenant,

en.L: and {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} confirmed it to Jacob as a statute, to Israel as an everlasting covenant,
en.B: and {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} set it in place for Jacob as a decree, for Israel as a covenant that lasts forever,
en.R: He made it a firm law for Jacob, a covenant with Israel that will last forever.

fr.L: et {{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} l’a établie pour Jacob comme une prescription, pour Israël comme une alliance éternelle,
fr.B: et {{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} l’a confirmée pour Jacob comme un décret, pour Israël comme une alliance qui dure toujours,
fr.R: Il en a fait une loi solide pour Jacob, une alliance avec Israël qui durera toujours.

sw.L: {{deity_pronoun:naye|Naye}} akalithibitisha kwa Yakobo kuwa kanuni, kwa Israeli [kuwa] agano la milele,
sw.B: {{deity_pronoun:naye|Naye}} akaliweka imara kwa Yakobo kuwa agizo, kwa Israeli kuwa agano linalodumu milele,
sw.R: Alilifanya kuwa sheria thabiti kwa Yakobo, agano na Israeli litakalodumu milele.

decisions.choice: the promise renewed to Jacob, also called Israel
decisions.reason: God renewed the promise of the land to Jacob at Bethel (Genesis 28:13-15; 35:11-12), where he also confirmed the name Israel (Genesis 35:10). The two names here are the same man.
The word (choq) is something laid down that does not change. God bound himself to his promise as firmly as a law.

decisions.choice: set it in place (B); made it a firm law (R)
decisions.reason: The verb (he'emid) is to make something stand; Balanced and Readable keep that picture of firmness.

source.text: לֵאמֹ֗ר לְךָ֗ אֶתֵּ֥ן אֶת־אֶֽרֶץ־כְּנָ֑עַן חֶ֝֗בֶל נַחֲלַתְכֶֽם׃

records.literal_gloss: saying: To you I will give the land of Canaan, [the] portion of your inheritance.

en.L: saying, "To you I will give the land of Canaan, the measured portion of your inheritance."
en.B: saying, "The land of Canaan I give to you, a share marked out for you to inherit."
en.R: He said, "The land of Canaan will be yours. I am giving it to you as your own share."

fr.L: en disant : « À toi je donnerai le pays de Canaan, la part mesurée de votre héritage. »
fr.B: en disant : « Je te donne le pays de Canaan, une part délimitée pour que vous en héritiez. »
fr.R: Il a dit : « Le pays de Canaan sera à vous. Je vous le donne pour qu’il soit votre part. »

sw.L: akisema, "Kwako nitakupa nchi ya Kanaani, fungu lililopimwa la urithi wenu."
sw.B: akisema, "Nchi ya Kanaani nakupa wewe, fungu lililopimiwa ninyi kuwa urithi wenu."
sw.R: Alisema, "Nchi ya Kanaani itakuwa yako. Nawapa ninyi kuwa fungu lenu wenyewe."

decisions.reason: God promised Canaan to Abraham and his offspring (Genesis 12:7; 13:15; 17:8) and to Jacob (Genesis 28:13).
"To you" is singular, spoken to each of the fathers; "your inheritance" is plural, the share of the whole people descended from them.

decisions.choice: portion: a share marked out with a line
decisions.reason: The word (chevel) is a measuring cord, and then the plot of land measured with it (16:6; Deuteronomy 32:9).
Readable starts a new sentence and names the speaker, God.

source.text: בִּֽ֭הְיוֹתָם מְתֵ֣י מִסְפָּ֑ר כִּ֝מְעַ֗ט וְגָרִ֥ים בָּֽהּ׃

records.literal_gloss: When they were men of number, like a few, and sojourners in it,

en.L: When they were men of [small] number, very few, and sojourners in it,
en.B: When they were only a handful of people, a few outsiders living in that land,
en.R: At that time there were only a few of them. They were foreigners living in Canaan.

fr.L: Quand ils étaient des hommes [en petit] nombre, une poignée, et qu’ils y étaient des immigrés,
fr.B: Quand ils n’étaient qu’une poignée de gens, quelques étrangers vivant dans ce pays,
fr.R: À cette époque-là, ils n’étaient pas nombreux. Ils vivaient en étrangers dans le pays de Canaan.

sw.L: Walipokuwa watu wa hesabu [ndogo], wachache sana, na wageni ndani yake,
sw.B: Walipokuwa kikundi kidogo tu cha watu, wageni wachache walioishi katika nchi ile,
sw.R: Wakati huo walikuwa wachache tu. Walikuwa wageni walioishi Kanaani.

decisions.choice: men of number: few, easily counted
decisions.reason: People who can be counted are few (Genesis 34:30; Deuteronomy 26:5, "few in number"). "Like a few" makes it stronger: very few indeed.

decisions.choice: sojourners: foreigners living in the land
decisions.reason: A sojourner (ger) lived in a land without owning it, under others' protection. Abraham called himself one in Canaan (Genesis 23:4).

decisions.choice: the "when" clause goes with what follows
decisions.reason: The clause can end the promise of verse 11 or begin the sentence that ends in verse 14; it is taken with verse 14: while they were few and wandering, God protected them. The parallel in 1 Chronicles 16:19 reads "when you were".
Readable names the land that "it" refers to.

decisions.choice: the history told in Psalms 105–107 is in the passé composé (with the imperfect for background) at every level
alternatives: passé simple at Literal and Balanced, as in the narrative books
decisions.reason: These psalms tell Israel's story inside a song addressed to the people and to God. Like the song of Exodus 15 and the retellings in the speeches of Acts, that is speech, so French uses the tenses of speech at every level.

source.text: וַֽ֭יִּתְהַלְּכוּ מִגּ֣וֹי אֶל־גּ֑וֹי מִ֝מַּמְלָכָ֗ה אֶל־עַ֥ם אַחֵֽר׃

records.literal_gloss: and they went about from nation to nation, from a kingdom to another people,

en.L: and they went about from nation to nation, from a kingdom to another people,
en.B: wandering from one nation to the next, from one kingdom to another people,
en.R: They wandered from one country to another, from one kingdom to the next.

fr.L: et qu’ils allaient de nation en nation, d’un royaume vers un autre peuple,
fr.B: errant d’une nation à l’autre, d’un royaume vers un autre peuple,
fr.R: Ils allaient d’un pays à l’autre, d’un royaume à un autre.

sw.L: nao walizunguka kutoka taifa hadi taifa, kutoka ufalme mmoja hadi kwa watu wengine,
sw.B: wakitangatanga kutoka taifa moja hadi jingine, kutoka ufalme mmoja hadi kwa watu wengine,
sw.R: Walitangatanga kutoka nchi moja hadi nyingine, kutoka ufalme mmoja hadi mwingine.

decisions.reason: Abraham went from Haran to Canaan and down to Egypt (Genesis 12:4-10) and lived in Gerar (Genesis 20:1); Isaac lived in Gerar (Genesis 26:6); Jacob went to Haran and back (Genesis 28-31) and at last to Egypt (Genesis 46:1-7).

decisions.choice: went about: walked here and there
decisions.reason: The verb (hithallekh) is to go to and fro, a life on the move without a land of one's own.

source.text: לֹֽא־הִנִּ֣יחַ אָדָ֣ם לְעָשְׁקָ֑ם וַיּ֖וֹכַח עֲלֵיהֶ֣ם מְלָכִֽים׃

records.literal_gloss: not he allowed a man to oppress them, and he rebuked on account of them kings:

en.L: {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} allowed no one to oppress them, and {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} rebuked kings on their account:
en.B: {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} let no one do them wrong, and {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} took kings to task over them:
en.R: But God did not let anyone treat them badly. He warned kings to leave them alone. He said,

fr.L: {{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} n’a permis à personne de les opprimer, et {{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} a réprimandé des rois à cause d’eux :
fr.B: {{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} n’a laissé personne leur faire du tort, et à cause d’eux {{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} a sévèrement averti des rois :
fr.R: Mais Dieu n’a laissé personne les maltraiter. Il a averti des rois de les laisser tranquilles. Il a dit :

sw.L: hakumruhusu mtu yeyote awaonee, na kwa ajili yao akawakemea wafalme:
sw.B: hakumwacha mtu yeyote awadhulumu, na kwa ajili yao akawakaripia wafalme:
sw.R: Lakini Mungu hakumwacha mtu yeyote awatendee mabaya. Aliwaonya wafalme wawaache. Alisema,

decisions.choice: kings rebuked for the fathers' sake
decisions.reason: God struck Pharaoh because of Sarah (Genesis 12:17), warned Abimelech king of Gerar in a dream (Genesis 20:3-7), and Abimelech later forbade anyone to harm Isaac (Genesis 26:11).
The word ('adam) here means any human being: no one at all.
Readable starts a new sentence, so it names God, and it introduces the words of verse 15 as his.

source.text: אַֽל־תִּגְּע֥וּ בִמְשִׁיחָ֑י וְ֝לִנְבִיאַי אַל־תָּרֵֽעוּ׃

records.literal_gloss: Do not touch my anointed [ones], and to my prophets do not do harm.

en.L: "Do not touch {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} anointed ones, and do no harm to {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} prophets."
en.B: "Do not lay a hand on {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} anointed ones; do not hurt {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} prophets."
en.R: "Do not harm the people I have set apart for {{deity_pronoun:myself|Myself}}. Do not hurt {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} prophets."

fr.L: « Ne touchez pas à {{deity_pronoun:mes|Mes}} oints, et ne faites pas de mal à {{deity_pronoun:mes|Mes}} prophètes. »
fr.B: « Ne portez pas la main sur {{deity_pronoun:mes|Mes}} oints ; ne faites pas de mal à {{deity_pronoun:mes|Mes}} prophètes. »
fr.R: « Ne faites pas de mal aux gens que j’ai mis à part pour {{deity_pronoun:moi|Moi}}. Ne maltraitez pas {{deity_pronoun:mes|Mes}} prophètes. »

sw.L: "Msiwaguse wapakwa mafuta {{deity_pronoun:wangu|Wangu}}, wala msiwadhuru manabii {{deity_pronoun:wangu|Wangu}}."
sw.B: "Msinyooshe mkono juu ya wapakwa mafuta {{deity_pronoun:wangu|Wangu}}; msiwaumize manabii {{deity_pronoun:wangu|Wangu}}."
sw.R: "Msiwadhuru watu niliowatenga kuwa {{deity_pronoun:wangu|Wangu}}. Msiwaumize manabii {{deity_pronoun:wangu|Wangu}}."

decisions.choice: my anointed ones: the fathers, set apart by God
decisions.reason: Kings and priests were anointed with oil. The fathers never were, but they were chosen and set apart by God as if anointed. This is the only place the word (mashiach) is used of them.
God calls Abraham a prophet who will pray for Abimelech (Genesis 20:7).

decisions.choice: the end of the parallel in 1 Chronicles 16
decisions.reason: 1 Chronicles 16:22 ends the shared lines here; the song there goes on with Psalm 96.

decisions.choice: the people I have set apart for myself
decisions.reason: Readable says what "anointed" means here (m1).

source.text: וַיִּקְרָ֣א רָ֭עָב עַל־הָאָ֑רֶץ כָּֽל־מַטֵּה־לֶ֥חֶם שָׁבָֽר׃

records.literal_gloss: And he called a famine on the land; every staff of bread he broke.

en.L: And {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} called a famine upon the land; every staff of bread {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} broke.
en.B: He summoned a famine over the land and broke off every supply of bread.
en.R: Then {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} sent a famine on the land and took away all their food.

fr.L: Et {{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} a appelé la famine sur le pays ; tout bâton de pain, {{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} [l’]a brisé.
fr.B: Il a convoqué la famine sur le pays et a coupé toutes les réserves de pain.
fr.R: Puis {{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} a envoyé une famine sur le pays et leur a enlevé toute leur nourriture.

sw.L: Naye akaita njaa juu ya nchi; kila tegemeo la mkate akalivunja.
sw.B: Aliita njaa iijie nchi, akaondoa kila akiba ya chakula.
sw.R: Kisha akaleta njaa juu ya nchi, akawaondolea chakula chao chote.

decisions.reason: The famine came on Egypt and Canaan, and Jacob's sons went down to buy grain (Genesis 41:54-57; 42:1-5).

decisions.choice: staff of bread: the food that supports life
decisions.reason: Bread is pictured as the staff a person leans on; to break it is to cut off the food supply (Leviticus 26:26; Ezekiel 4:16).
The famine is summoned like a servant who comes at its master's call (2 Kings 8:1).

decisions.choice: every supply of bread (B); all their food (R)
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable say what the picture means (m2).

source.text: שָׁלַ֣ח לִפְנֵיהֶ֣ם אִ֑ישׁ לְ֝עֶ֗בֶד נִמְכַּ֥ר יוֹסֵֽף׃

records.literal_gloss: He sent before them a man; as a slave he was sold, Joseph.

en.L: He sent a man before them; Joseph was sold as a slave.
en.B: But {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} had already sent a man on ahead of them: Joseph, who was sold to be a slave.
en.R: But {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} had already sent a man ahead of them to Egypt. That man was Joseph, who had been sold as a slave.

fr.L: Il a envoyé devant eux un homme ; comme esclave il a été vendu, Joseph.
fr.B: Mais {{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} avait déjà envoyé un homme en avant d’eux : Joseph, qui a été vendu comme esclave.
fr.R: Mais {{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} avait déjà envoyé un homme en Égypte avant eux. Cet homme, c’était Joseph, qui avait été vendu comme esclave.

sw.L: Alimtuma mtu mbele yao; Yusufu aliuzwa kuwa mtumwa.
sw.B: Lakini alikuwa amekwisha kumtuma mtu awatangulie: Yusufu, aliyeuzwa awe mtumwa.
sw.R: Lakini alikuwa amekwisha kumtuma mtu awatangulie kwenda Misri. Mtu huyo alikuwa Yusufu, aliyekuwa ameuzwa kama mtumwa.

decisions.reason: Joseph's brothers sold him and he was taken to Egypt (Genesis 37:28, 36). Later he told them, "God sent me before you to keep you alive" (Genesis 45:5-8).
The same event is told two ways: his brothers sold him, but God sent him. The psalm, like Genesis 50:20, sees God's purpose in what people did wrongly.
Joseph was sent before the famine began, so Balanced and Readable make the order of events plain.
Readable names where Joseph was sent.
"Slave" at every level, as the style guide keeps it where people are bought or sold: Joseph was sold (m1; Genesis 37:28).
Joseph was sold, so real slavery is meant; "mtumishi" would hide that he was bought and owned.

source.text: עִנּ֣וּ בַכֶּ֣בֶל רַגְל֑וֹ בַּ֝רְזֶ֗ל בָּ֣אָה נַפְשֽׁוֹ׃

records.literal_gloss: They afflicted with the fetter[s] his feet; [into] iron came his neck,

en.L: They afflicted his feet with fetters; his neck came into iron,
en.B: Shackles bruised his feet, and his neck was locked in iron,
en.R: His feet were hurt by chains, and an iron collar was put around his neck.

fr.L: On a meurtri ses pieds avec des entraves ; son cou est entré dans le fer,
fr.B: Les fers ont blessé ses pieds, et son cou a été pris dans un collier de fer,
fr.R: On lui a fait mal aux pieds avec des chaînes, et on lui a mis un collier de fer autour du cou.

sw.L: Waliitesa miguu yake kwa pingu; shingo yake iliingia katika chuma,
sw.B: Pingu ziliichubua miguu yake, na shingo yake ilifungwa kwa chuma,
sw.R: Miguu yake iliumizwa na minyororo, naye akavishwa pete ya chuma shingoni.

decisions.reason: The Hebrew text notes a difference here between what is written and what is to be read; the words follow the form to be read.
The word (nefesh) can mean the throat or neck (69:2), and so the picture is an iron collar. The old rendering "iron entered his soul" takes it as his inner self.
Joseph was put in the prison where the king's prisoners were held (Genesis 39:20; 40:15). Genesis does not mention chains; the psalm shows his suffering there.

source.text: עַד־עֵ֥ת בֹּֽא־דְבָר֑וֹ אִמְרַ֖ת יְהוָ֣ה צְרָפָֽתְהוּ׃

records.literal_gloss: until [the] time of [the] coming of his word, the saying of YHWH tested him.

en.L: until the time that his word came, the saying of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} tested him.
en.B: until the day his own words came true; the word of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} refined him.
en.R: This lasted until what Joseph had said came true. What {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} had said tested him, as fire tests metal.

fr.L: jusqu’au temps où sa parole est arrivée ; la parole {{divine_name:du SEIGNEUR|de Yahvé}} l’a éprouvé.
fr.B: jusqu’au jour où ses propres paroles se sont réalisées ; la parole {{divine_name:du SEIGNEUR|de Yahvé}} l’a purifié comme un métal.
fr.R: Cela a duré jusqu’au jour où ce que Joseph avait annoncé s’est réalisé. Ce que {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} avait dit l’a mis à l’épreuve, comme le feu éprouve le métal.

sw.L: mpaka wakati neno lake lilipotimia, tamko la {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} lilimjaribu.
sw.B: mpaka siku maneno yake yenyewe yalipotimia; neno la {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} lilimsafisha.
sw.R: Hali hiyo iliendelea mpaka yale aliyoyasema Yusufu yalipotimia. Neno la {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} lilimjaribu, kama moto unavyojaribu chuma.

decisions.reason: "His word" is taken as what Joseph had said when he explained the dreams in prison and before Pharaoh (Genesis 40:12-22; 41:25-36), which came true. It may instead be God's word, in parallel with "the saying of the LORD".

decisions.choice: tested: refined, as metal in fire
decisions.reason: The verb (tsaraf) is used of refining silver (12:7; 66:10). God's word, given through the dreams, tried Joseph until it was fulfilled.
Readable names whose words came true and spells out the picture of refining (m1, m2).

source.text: שָׁ֣לַח מֶ֭לֶךְ וַיַּתִּירֵ֑הוּ מֹשֵׁ֥ל עַ֝מִּ֗ים וַֽיְפַתְּחֵֽהוּ׃

records.literal_gloss: [A] king sent and released him, [the] ruler of peoples, and set him free.

en.L: [The] king sent and released him, the ruler of peoples, and set him free.
en.B: The king sent orders to free him; the ruler of many peoples let him loose.
en.R: Then the king of Egypt sent for Joseph and had him freed. The ruler of many nations let him go.

fr.L: [Le] roi a envoyé [quelqu’un] et l’a délié, le souverain des peuples, et l’a libéré.
fr.B: Le roi a donné l’ordre de le libérer ; le souverain de nombreux peuples l’a relâché.
fr.R: Alors le roi d’Égypte a fait chercher Joseph et l’a fait libérer. Le souverain de nombreuses nations l’a laissé partir.

sw.L: Mfalme alituma akamfungua, mtawala wa mataifa, akamwacha huru.
sw.B: Mfalme alituma watu wamfungue; mtawala wa mataifa mengi akamwachilia.
sw.R: Kisha mfalme wa Misri alimwita Yusufu, akaamuru afunguliwe. Mtawala wa mataifa mengi alimwachilia aende.

decisions.reason: Pharaoh sent and called Joseph, and they brought him quickly out of the dungeon (Genesis 41:14).

decisions.choice: set him free: loosed his bonds
decisions.reason: The verb (pittach) is to loosen or open, as of chains (116:16).
Readable names the king's land and the man he freed.

source.text: שָׂמ֣וֹ אָד֣וֹן לְבֵית֑וֹ וּ֝מֹשֵׁ֗ל בְּכָל־קִנְיָנֽוֹ׃

records.literal_gloss: He made him lord of his house and ruler over all his possession,

en.L: He made him lord of his house and ruler over all his property,
en.B: He put him in charge of his palace and gave him rule over all his wealth,
en.R: Pharaoh put Joseph in charge of his palace and of everything he owned.

fr.L: Il l’a établi seigneur de sa maison et gouverneur de tous ses biens,
fr.B: Il lui a confié son palais et lui a donné autorité sur toutes ses richesses,
fr.R: Le pharaon a mis Joseph à la tête de son palais et de tout ce qu’il possédait.

sw.L: Alimfanya bwana wa nyumba yake na mtawala juu ya mali yake yote,
sw.B: Alimweka kuwa msimamizi wa jumba lake la kifalme, akampa mamlaka juu ya mali yake yote,
sw.R: Farao alimweka Yusufu kuwa msimamizi wa jumba lake la kifalme na wa kila kitu alichokuwa nacho.

decisions.reason: Pharaoh set Joseph over his house and over all the land of Egypt (Genesis 41:40-44; 45:8).
The king of verse 20 is the subject; "him" is Joseph and "his" the king's.
Readable names who did what.

source.text: לֶאְסֹ֣ר שָׂרָ֣יו בְּנַפְשׁ֑וֹ וּזְקֵנָ֥יו יְחַכֵּֽם׃

records.literal_gloss: to bind his princes at his will, and his elders he made wise.

en.L: to bind his princes at his will and to make his elders wise.
en.B: with power to put his officials in chains if he chose, and to make his counselors wise.
en.R: Joseph could even have the king's officials arrested if he wanted. He taught the king's advisers to be wise.

fr.L: pour lier ses princes à son gré et rendre sages ses anciens.
fr.B: avec le pouvoir de mettre aux fers ses hauts fonctionnaires s’il le voulait, et d’enseigner la sagesse à ses conseillers.
fr.R: Joseph pouvait même faire arrêter les fonctionnaires du roi s’il le voulait. Il a appris aux conseillers du roi à être sages.

sw.L: kuwafunga wakuu wake kwa mapenzi yake, na kuwafanya wazee wake wawe na hekima.
sw.B: akiwa na mamlaka ya kuwatia maafisa wake minyororo akipenda, na kuwafundisha washauri wake hekima.
sw.R: Yusufu aliweza hata kuamuru maafisa wa mfalme wakamatwe akitaka. Aliwafundisha washauri wa mfalme kuwa na hekima.

decisions.reason: The Hebrew reads "to bind", that is, Joseph had power even to imprison Pharaoh's officials. The ancient Greek and Syriac translations read "to instruct", which matches the second line and differs in Hebrew by one letter.

decisions.choice: at his will: as he wished
decisions.reason: The word (nefesh) here is desire or will: Joseph acted as he saw fit, with the king's authority (Genesis 41:44).
The elders are the senior men of Pharaoh's court (Genesis 50:7).
Readable names the people, since "his" refers to two men in these verses.

source.text: וַיָּבֹ֣א יִשְׂרָאֵ֣ל מִצְרָ֑יִם וְ֝יַעֲקֹ֗ב גָּ֣ר בְּאֶֽרֶץ־חָֽם׃

records.literal_gloss: And Israel came [to] Egypt, and Jacob sojourned in [the] land of Ham.

en.L: And Israel came [into] Egypt; Jacob sojourned in the land of Ham.
en.B: So Israel came into Egypt, and Jacob settled as a guest in the land of Ham.
en.R: Then Jacob and his family came to Egypt. They lived there as foreigners, in the land of Ham.

fr.L: Et Israël est venu [en] Égypte ; Jacob a séjourné dans le pays de Cham.
fr.B: Ainsi Israël est entré en Égypte, et Jacob s’est installé comme un hôte dans le pays de Cham.
fr.R: Puis Jacob et sa famille sont venus en Égypte. Ils y ont vécu comme des étrangers, dans le pays de Cham.

sw.L: Naye Israeli akaingia Misri; Yakobo akakaa kama mgeni katika nchi ya Hamu.
sw.B: Ndipo Israeli akaingia Misri, na Yakobo akakaa kama mgeni katika nchi ya Hamu.
sw.R: Kisha Yakobo na jamaa yake walikuja Misri. Waliishi huko kama wageni, katika nchi ya Hamu.

decisions.reason: Jacob, also called Israel, went down to Egypt with all his family and settled in Goshen (Genesis 46:1-7; 47:27).
Ham was the father of Mizraim, that is, Egypt (Genesis 10:6), so Egypt is called the land of Ham (78:51).
The two names are one man, who came with his whole household; Readable says this once instead of using both names.

source.text: וַיֶּ֣פֶר אֶת־עַמּ֣וֹ מְאֹ֑ד וַ֝יַּֽעֲצִמֵהוּ מִצָּרָֽיו׃

records.literal_gloss: And he made fruitful his people greatly, and made them stronger than their foes.

en.L: And {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} made {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} people very fruitful and made them stronger than their foes.
en.B: There {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} made {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} people grow greatly in number, until they were too strong for their enemies.
en.R: There {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} made {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} people grow into a large nation, stronger than their enemies.

fr.L: Et {{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} a rendu {{deity_pronoun:son|Son}} peuple très fécond et l’a rendu plus fort que ses adversaires.
fr.B: Là, {{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} a fait croître {{deity_pronoun:son|Son}} peuple en grand nombre, jusqu’à le rendre trop fort pour ses ennemis.
fr.R: Là, {{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} a fait de {{deity_pronoun:son|Son}} peuple une grande nation, plus forte que ses ennemis.

sw.L: Naye akawazidisha sana watu {{deity_pronoun:wake|Wake}}, akawafanya wenye nguvu kuliko adui zao.
sw.B: Huko aliwafanya watu {{deity_pronoun:wake|Wake}} waongezeke sana kwa idadi, hata wakawa na nguvu kuliko adui zao.
sw.R: Huko aliwakuza watu {{deity_pronoun:wake|Wake}} wakawa taifa kubwa, wenye nguvu kuliko adui zao.

decisions.reason: The Israelites were fruitful, multiplied and grew very strong, so that the land was filled with them (Exodus 1:7, 9).

decisions.choice: made them stronger: mighty, or numerous
decisions.reason: The verb ('atsam) is to be strong or to be many; both are in view in Exodus 1:9.

source.text: הָפַ֣ךְ לִ֭בָּם לִשְׂנֹ֣א עַמּ֑וֹ לְ֝הִתְנַכֵּ֗ל בַּעֲבָדָֽיו׃

records.literal_gloss: He turned their heart to hate his people, to deal craftily with his servants.

en.L: He turned their heart to hate {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} people, to deal craftily with {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} servants.
en.B: He turned the hearts of the Egyptians to hatred of {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} people and to scheming against {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} servants.
en.R: He let the Egyptians come to hate {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} people. They made sly plans against {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} servants.

fr.L: Il a tourné leur cœur à haïr {{deity_pronoun:son|Son}} peuple, à agir avec ruse envers {{deity_pronoun:ses|Ses}} esclaves.
fr.B: Il a tourné le cœur des Égyptiens vers la haine de {{deity_pronoun:son|Son}} peuple et vers les complots contre {{deity_pronoun:ses|Ses}} serviteurs.
fr.R: Il a laissé les Égyptiens se mettre à détester {{deity_pronoun:son|Son}} peuple. Ils ont fait des plans rusés contre {{deity_pronoun:ses|Ses}} serviteurs.

sw.L: Aliugeuza moyo wao wawachukie watu {{deity_pronoun:wake|Wake}}, wawatendee hila watumishi {{deity_pronoun:wake|Wake}}.
sw.B: Aliigeuza mioyo ya Wamisri wawachukie watu {{deity_pronoun:wake|Wake}} na kuwafanyia hila watumishi {{deity_pronoun:wake|Wake}}.
sw.R: Aliwaacha Wamisri wawachukie watu {{deity_pronoun:wake|Wake}}. Walipanga mipango ya hila dhidi ya watumishi {{deity_pronoun:wake|Wake}}.

decisions.reason: A new king feared the Israelites and said, "Come, let us deal shrewdly with them", and made them slaves (Exodus 1:8-14).
The psalm sees God's hand even in Egypt's hatred, as Exodus speaks of the LORD hardening Pharaoh's heart (Exodus 4:21; 7:3). It does not excuse Egypt; it says nothing was outside God's rule.
Balanced and Readable name whose hearts were turned.
Readable keeps God as the one acting but in plainer words.

source.text: שָׁ֭לַח מֹשֶׁ֣ה עַבְדּ֑וֹ אַ֝הֲרֹ֗ן אֲשֶׁ֣ר בָּֽחַר־בּֽוֹ׃

records.literal_gloss: He sent Moses his servant, Aaron whom he had chosen.

en.L: He sent Moses {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} servant, Aaron whom {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} had chosen.
en.B: He sent {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} servant Moses, and with him Aaron, {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} chosen one.
en.R: Then {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} sent {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} servant Moses, along with Aaron, whom {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} had picked.

fr.L: Il a envoyé Moïse, {{deity_pronoun:son|Son}} serviteur, Aaron qu’{{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} avait choisi.
fr.B: Il a envoyé {{deity_pronoun:son|Son}} serviteur Moïse, et avec lui Aaron, {{deity_pronoun:son|Son}} élu.
fr.R: Puis {{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} a envoyé {{deity_pronoun:son|Son}} serviteur Moïse, avec Aaron, qu’{{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} avait choisi.

sw.L: Alimtuma Musa mtumishi {{deity_pronoun:wake|Wake}}, Haruni ambaye alikuwa amemchagua.
sw.B: Alimtuma mtumishi {{deity_pronoun:wake|Wake}} Musa, na pamoja naye Haruni, mteule {{deity_pronoun:wake|Wake}}.
sw.R: Kisha akamtuma mtumishi {{deity_pronoun:wake|Wake}} Musa, pamoja na Haruni, aliyekuwa amemchagua.

decisions.choice: Moses and Aaron sent to Pharaoh
decisions.reason: God sent Moses to Pharaoh (Exodus 3:10) and gave him Aaron to speak for him (Exodus 4:14-16, 27-28). Aaron's choosing was later shown by his staff that budded (Numbers 17).

decisions.choice: his servant: the title of Moses
decisions.reason: Moses is "the servant of the LORD" (Numbers 12:7; Deuteronomy 34:5).

source.text: שָֽׂמוּ־בָ֭ם דִּבְרֵ֣י אֹתוֹתָ֑יו וּ֝מֹפְתִ֗ים בְּאֶ֣רֶץ חָֽם׃

records.literal_gloss: They set among them [the] words of his signs, and wonders in [the] land of Ham.

en.L: They set among them the words of {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} signs, and wonders in the land of Ham.
en.B: Among the Egyptians they carried out the signs {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} had spoken of, and wonders throughout the land of Ham.
en.R: They did the miraculous signs {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} told them to do. They did amazing things in Egypt, the land of Ham.

fr.L: Ils ont placé parmi eux les paroles de {{deity_pronoun:ses|Ses}} signes, et des prodiges dans le pays de Cham.
fr.B: Chez les Égyptiens, ils ont accompli les signes qu’{{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} avait annoncés, et des prodiges dans tout le pays de Cham.
fr.R: Ils ont fait les signes miraculeux qu’{{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} leur avait demandé de faire. Ils ont fait des choses étonnantes en Égypte, le pays de Cham.

sw.L: Waliweka kati yao maneno ya ishara {{deity_pronoun:zake|Zake}}, na maajabu katika nchi ya Hamu.
sw.B: Kati ya Wamisri walizifanya ishara alizokuwa amezisema, na maajabu katika nchi yote ya Hamu.
sw.R: Walifanya ishara za miujiza alizowaambia wazifanye. Walifanya mambo ya ajabu huko Misri, nchi ya Hamu.

decisions.choice: the words of his signs: the signs he had spoken
decisions.reason: "Words" (devarim) can mean things or matters; here the signs are what God had told Moses to do (Exodus 4:28; 7:2).
The Hebrew says that Moses and Aaron performed the signs. The ancient Greek and Syriac translations read "he set", with God as the one acting, as in Psalm 78:43.
Balanced and Readable name who "them" are.

source.text: שָׁ֣לַֽח חֹ֭שֶׁךְ וַיַּחְשִׁ֑ךְ וְלֹֽא־מָ֝ר֗וּ אֶת־דְּבָרֽוֹ׃

records.literal_gloss: He sent darkness and made [it] dark, and not they rebelled against his word.

en.L: He sent darkness and made [it] dark, and they did not rebel against {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} word.
en.B: He sent darkness and the land went dark; and they did not defy {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} word.
en.R: He sent darkness and made the land dark. Moses and Aaron did not go against what {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} said.

fr.L: Il a envoyé les ténèbres et a fait l’obscurité, et ils ne se sont pas rebellés contre {{deity_pronoun:sa|Sa}} parole.
fr.B: Il a envoyé les ténèbres, et le pays est devenu sombre ; et ils n’ont pas résisté à {{deity_pronoun:sa|Sa}} parole.
fr.R: Il a envoyé l’obscurité, et le pays est devenu tout noir. Moïse et Aaron n’ont pas désobéi à ce qu’{{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} avait dit.

sw.L: Alituma giza akafanya [kuwe na] giza, nao hawakuliasi neno {{deity_pronoun:lake|Lake}}.
sw.B: Alituma giza, nchi ikawa na giza; nao hawakulipinga neno {{deity_pronoun:lake|Lake}}.
sw.R: Alituma giza, akaifanya nchi iwe na giza. Musa na Haruni hawakwenda kinyume na yale aliyosema.

decisions.choice: darkness: the ninth plague, told first
decisions.reason: Thick darkness covered Egypt for three days (Exodus 10:21-23). The psalm begins its list with it and then tells seven more plagues in a different order from Exodus; the plagues on the livestock and the boils are not mentioned.

decisions.choice: they did not rebel: Moses and Aaron obeyed
decisions.reason: "They" are most simply Moses and Aaron, who did all that God commanded (Exodus 7:6). Some take it of the Egyptians or as a question. The ancient Greek and Syriac translations have no "not": "for they rebelled against his words".
The Hebrew text notes a difference here between what is written and what is to be read; the words follow the form to be read.
Readable names "they" as taken in m2.

source.text: הָפַ֣ךְ אֶת־מֵימֵיהֶ֣ם לְדָ֑ם וַ֝יָּ֗מֶת אֶת־דְּגָתָֽם׃

records.literal_gloss: He turned their waters into blood and caused their fish to die.

en.L: He turned their waters into blood and caused their fish to die.
en.B: He made their waters blood and left their fish dead.
en.R: He turned their rivers into blood, and the fish died.

fr.L: Il a changé leurs eaux en sang et a fait mourir leurs poissons.
fr.B: Il a fait de leurs eaux du sang et a laissé leurs poissons morts.
fr.R: Il a changé leurs rivières en sang, et les poissons sont morts.

sw.L: Aligeuza maji yao kuwa damu, akawaua samaki wao.
sw.B: Aliyafanya maji yao kuwa damu, akawaacha samaki wao wamekufa.
sw.R: Aligeuza mito yao kuwa damu, na samaki wakafa.

decisions.choice: water to blood: the first plague
decisions.reason: The water of the Nile became blood and the fish in it died (Exodus 7:17-21).

source.text: שָׁרַ֣ץ אַרְצָ֣ם צְפַרְדְּעִ֑ים בְּ֝חַדְרֵ֗י מַלְכֵיהֶֽם׃

records.literal_gloss: Their land swarmed [with] frogs, in the rooms of their kings.

en.L: Their land swarmed [with] frogs, in the chambers of their kings.
en.B: Frogs swarmed over their land, even into the inner rooms of their kings.
en.R: Frogs filled their land. They even got into the king's bedrooms.

fr.L: Leur pays a grouillé [de] grenouilles, jusque dans les chambres de leurs rois.
fr.B: Les grenouilles ont envahi leur pays, jusque dans les chambres de leurs rois.
fr.R: Il y a eu des grenouilles partout dans leur pays. Elles sont même entrées dans les chambres du roi.

sw.L: Nchi yao ilijaa vyura, katika vyumba vya wafalme wao.
sw.B: Vyura walijaa katika nchi yao, hata ndani ya vyumba vya ndani vya wafalme wao.
sw.R: Vyura walijaa nchi yao. Waliingia hata katika vyumba vya kulala vya mfalme.

decisions.reason: The frogs came up into Pharaoh's house, his bedroom and his bed (Exodus 8).
The plural may mean Pharaoh and his household, or the kings of Egypt in general; Exodus names Pharaoh's own rooms.
The word (cheder) is an inner or private room (Genesis 43:30), often a bedroom; Exodus 8 names Pharaoh's bedroom.

source.text: אָ֭מַר וַיָּבֹ֣א עָרֹ֑ב כִּ֝נִּ֗ים בְּכָל־גְּבוּלָֽם׃

records.literal_gloss: He spoke, and there came swarm[s], gnats in all their territory.

en.L: He spoke, and swarms came, gnats in all their territory.
en.B: At {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} command came swarms of flies, and gnats covered every part of their land.
en.R: He gave the order, and swarms of flies came. Gnats filled the whole country.

fr.L: Il a parlé, et des essaims sont venus, des moucherons dans tout leur territoire.
fr.B: Sur {{deity_pronoun:son|Son}} ordre sont venus des essaims de mouches, et des moucherons ont couvert tout leur pays.
fr.R: Il a donné l’ordre, et des essaims de mouches sont arrivés. Des moucherons ont rempli tout le pays.

sw.L: Alisema, na yakaja makundi [ya inzi], mbu katika mipaka yao yote.
sw.B: Kwa amri {{deity_pronoun:yake|Yake}} yalikuja makundi ya inzi, na mbu wakaenea kila sehemu ya nchi yao.
sw.R: Alitoa amri, na makundi ya inzi yakaja. Mbu walijaa nchi nzima.

decisions.choice: flies and gnats: the third and fourth plagues
decisions.reason: The dust became gnats, and then swarms filled the houses of Egypt (Exodus 8).
The word ('arov) names a swarm, traditionally of flies (78:45).
The word (kinnim) is a small biting insect; the exact kind is not known.
Balanced and Readable say what kind of swarm (m2).

source.text: נָתַ֣ן גִּשְׁמֵיהֶ֣ם בָּרָ֑ד אֵ֖שׁ לֶהָב֣וֹת בְּאַרְצָֽם׃

records.literal_gloss: He gave [as] their rains hail, fire of flames in their land.

en.L: He gave them hail [for] rain, flaming fire in their land.
en.B: Instead of rain {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} gave them hail, with fire flashing across their land.
en.R: Instead of rain, {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} sent hail, and lightning flashed all over their land.

fr.L: Il leur a donné [pour] pluies la grêle, un feu de flammes dans leur pays.
fr.B: Au lieu de pluie, {{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} leur a donné de la grêle, avec un feu qui flamboyait sur leur pays.
fr.R: Au lieu de pluie, {{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} a envoyé de la grêle, et les éclairs ont brillé partout dans leur pays.

sw.L: Aliwapa mvua ya mawe [badala ya] mvua, moto wa miali katika nchi yao.
sw.B: Badala ya mvua aliwapa mvua ya mawe, na moto ukimulika katika nchi yao yote.
sw.R: Badala ya mvua, alileta mvua ya mawe, na radi zikamulika kila mahali katika nchi yao.

decisions.reason: The LORD sent thunder and hail, and fire ran down to the ground, fire flashing in the hail (Exodus 9:23-24).
Fire coming down with the hail is lightning (Exodus 9:23).
"He gave their rains hail" means the rain they would have had came as hail; Balanced and Readable say so.

source.text: וַיַּ֣ךְ גַּ֭פְנָם וּתְאֵנָתָ֑ם וַ֝יְשַׁבֵּ֗ר עֵ֣ץ גְּבוּלָֽם׃

records.literal_gloss: And he struck their vine[s] and their fig tree[s], and broke [the] tree[s] of their territory.

en.L: And {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} struck their vines and their fig trees, and shattered the trees of their territory.
en.B: He beat down their grapevines and their fig trees and splintered every tree in their land.
en.R: He destroyed their grapevines and fig trees and broke down the trees all over their country.

fr.L: Et {{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} a frappé leurs vignes et leurs figuiers, et a brisé les arbres de leur territoire.
fr.B: Il a abattu leurs vignes et leurs figuiers et a fracassé tous les arbres de leur pays.
fr.R: Il a détruit leurs vignes et leurs figuiers et a cassé les arbres dans tout le pays.

sw.L: Naye akaipiga mizabibu yao na mitini yao, akaivunja miti ya mipaka yao.
sw.B: Aliiangusha mizabibu yao na mitini yao, akaivunjavunja miti yote ya nchi yao.
sw.R: Aliharibu mizabibu yao na mitini, akavunja miti kila mahali katika nchi yao.

decisions.reason: The hail struck every plant of the field and broke every tree (Exodus 9:25).

source.text: אָ֭מַר וַיָּבֹ֣א אַרְבֶּ֑ה וְ֝יֶ֗לֶק וְאֵ֣ין מִסְפָּֽר׃

records.literal_gloss: He spoke, and there came locust[s], and young locust[s], and there was no number,

en.L: He spoke, and locusts came, and young locusts without number,
en.B: At {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} word the locusts arrived, swarms of young locusts too many to count,
en.R: He gave the word, and locusts came, more than anyone could count.

fr.L: Il a parlé, et des sauterelles sont venues, et des criquets sans nombre,
fr.B: À {{deity_pronoun:sa|Sa}} parole les sauterelles sont arrivées, des essaims de jeunes criquets impossibles à compter,
fr.R: Il a donné l’ordre, et des sauterelles sont venues, si nombreuses que personne ne pouvait les compter.

sw.L: Alisema, na nzige wakaja, na tunutu bila hesabu,
sw.B: Kwa neno {{deity_pronoun:lake|Lake}} nzige walifika, makundi ya tunutu wasiohesabika,
sw.R: Alitoa neno, na nzige wakaja, wengi kuliko mtu yeyote angeweza kuhesabu.

decisions.reason: Locusts covered the land and ate what the hail had left (Exodus 10:12-15).
The word (yeleq) is a kind of locust, probably the young, wingless stage (Joel 1:4 names it with others; Nahum 3:15).
Readable uses one word for both kinds of locust.

source.text: וַיֹּ֣אכַל כָּל־עֵ֣שֶׂב בְּאַרְצָ֑ם וַ֝יֹּ֗אכַל פְּרִ֣י אַדְמָתָֽם׃

records.literal_gloss: and it ate all [the] vegetation in their land, and it ate [the] fruit of their ground.

en.L: and they ate up all the vegetation in their land, and ate up the fruit of their ground.
en.B: and they devoured every green plant in their land and swallowed up the harvest of their fields.
en.R: They ate every plant in the land and all the crops in the fields.

fr.L: et elles ont dévoré toute la verdure dans leur pays, et ont dévoré le fruit de leur sol.
fr.B: et elles ont dévoré toute plante verte dans leur pays et englouti la récolte de leurs champs.
fr.R: Elles ont mangé toutes les plantes du pays et toutes les récoltes des champs.

sw.L: nao wakala kila mmea katika nchi yao, wakala matunda ya ardhi yao.
sw.B: nao wakala kila mmea wa kijani katika nchi yao, wakayameza mavuno ya mashamba yao.
sw.R: Walikula kila mmea nchini na mazao yote mashambani.

decisions.reason: The locusts ate every plant and all the fruit of the trees; nothing green remained in Egypt (Exodus 10:15).

decisions.choice: it ate: the swarm as one
decisions.reason: The verb is singular, treating the swarm as one devouring mass; the sense is plural.

source.text: וַיַּ֣ךְ כָּל־בְּכ֣וֹר בְּאַרְצָ֑ם רֵ֝אשִׁ֗ית לְכָל־אוֹנָֽם׃

records.literal_gloss: And he struck every firstborn in their land, [the] first of all their strength.

en.L: And {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} struck down every firstborn in their land, the first of all their strength.
en.B: And {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} killed the firstborn of every family in their land, the first sons born of their strength.
en.R: Then {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} struck down the firstborn in every home in Egypt, the first child each father had.

fr.L: Et {{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} a frappé tout premier-né dans leur pays, les prémices de toute leur vigueur.
fr.B: Et {{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} a fait mourir le premier-né de chaque famille dans leur pays, les premiers fils nés de leur vigueur.
fr.R: Puis {{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} a frappé à mort le premier-né dans chaque maison d’Égypte, le premier enfant de chaque père.

sw.L: Naye akampiga kila mzaliwa wa kwanza katika nchi yao, malimbuko ya nguvu zao zote.
sw.B: Naye akamwua mzaliwa wa kwanza wa kila familia katika nchi yao, wana wa kwanza waliozaliwa kwa nguvu zao.
sw.R: Kisha akamwua mzaliwa wa kwanza katika kila nyumba huko Misri, mtoto wa kwanza wa kila baba.

decisions.choice: the death of the firstborn: the tenth plague
decisions.reason: At midnight the LORD struck down every firstborn in Egypt, from Pharaoh's son to the cattle (Exodus 12:29).

decisions.choice: the first of all their strength: the firstborn son
decisions.reason: The firstborn is "the first of a man's strength", the first fruit of his manhood (Genesis 49:3; Deuteronomy 21:17). Psalm 78:51 uses almost the same words.

decisions.choice: the first sons born of their strength (B); the first child each father had (R)
alternatives: the first of all their strength
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable make the idiom plain (m2).

source.text: וַֽ֭יּוֹצִיאֵם בְּכֶ֣סֶף וְזָהָ֑ב וְאֵ֖ין בִּשְׁבָטָ֣יו כּוֹשֵֽׁל׃

records.literal_gloss: And he brought them out with silver and gold, and there was not among his tribes [one who] stumbled.

en.L: And {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} brought them out with silver and gold, and among {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} tribes [there was] none who stumbled.
en.B: He brought {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} people out carrying silver and gold, and in all {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} tribes not one person stumbled.
en.R: He led {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} people out of Egypt with silver and gold. Not one person in {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} tribes was too weak to walk.

fr.L: Et {{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} les a fait sortir avec de l’argent et de l’or, et parmi {{deity_pronoun:ses|Ses}} tribus [il n’y avait] personne qui chancelait.
fr.B: Il a fait sortir {{deity_pronoun:son|Son}} peuple chargé d’argent et d’or, et dans toutes {{deity_pronoun:ses|Ses}} tribus personne n’a trébuché.
fr.R: Il a fait sortir {{deity_pronoun:son|Son}} peuple d’Égypte avec de l’argent et de l’or. Dans {{deity_pronoun:ses|Ses}} tribus, personne n’était trop faible pour marcher.

sw.L: Naye akawatoa pamoja na fedha na dhahabu, wala katika makabila {{deity_pronoun:yake|Yake}} hapakuwa na aliyejikwaa.
sw.B: Aliwatoa watu {{deity_pronoun:wake|Wake}} wakiwa wamebeba fedha na dhahabu, na katika makabila {{deity_pronoun:yake|Yake}} yote hakuna hata mtu mmoja aliyejikwaa.
sw.R: Aliwaongoza watu {{deity_pronoun:wake|Wake}} kutoka Misri wakiwa na fedha na dhahabu. Hakuna hata mtu mmoja katika makabila {{deity_pronoun:yake|Yake}} aliyekuwa dhaifu kiasi cha kushindwa kutembea.

decisions.choice: silver and gold from the Egyptians
decisions.reason: The Israelites asked the Egyptians for silver and gold, and the LORD made the Egyptians willing to give it (Exodus 11:2-3; 12:35-36), as promised to Abraham (Genesis 15:14).
"His" is taken as God's, as "his people" and "his chosen ones" throughout the psalm; it may also refer to Israel, the people as one man.
The word (koshel) is one who stumbles from weakness (Isaiah 5:27): all were strong enough for the journey.
Balanced and Readable name who was brought out.

source.text: שָׂמַ֣ח מִצְרַ֣יִם בְּצֵאתָ֑ם כִּֽי־נָפַ֖ל פַּחְדָּ֣ם עֲלֵיהֶֽם׃

records.literal_gloss: Egypt rejoiced when they went out, for [the] dread of them had fallen on them.

en.L: Egypt rejoiced when they went out, for the dread of them had fallen upon them.
en.B: Egypt was happy to see them go, since fear of them had come over its people.
en.R: The Egyptians were glad when Israel left, because they had become afraid of them.

fr.L: L’Égypte s’est réjouie quand ils sont sortis, car la terreur d’eux était tombée sur eux.
fr.B: L’Égypte a été contente de les voir partir, car la peur qu’ils inspiraient s’était emparée de ses habitants.
fr.R: Les Égyptiens étaient contents quand Israël est parti, parce qu’ils s’étaient mis à avoir peur d’eux.

sw.L: Misri ilifurahi walipotoka, kwa maana hofu yao ilikuwa imewaangukia.
sw.B: Misri ilifurahi kuwaona wakiondoka, kwa kuwa watu wake walikuwa wameingiwa na hofu yao.
sw.R: Wamisri walifurahi Waisraeli walipoondoka, kwa sababu walikuwa wamewaogopa.

decisions.reason: After the death of the firstborn the Egyptians urged the people to leave quickly, saying "we are all dead men" (Exodus 12:33).

decisions.choice: dread fell on them: they were seized with fear
decisions.reason: Fear is pictured as falling on people from outside (Exodus 15:16).
Readable names who left, since "they" and "them" refer to two peoples here.

source.text: פָּרַ֣שׂ עָנָ֣ן לְמָסָ֑ךְ וְ֝אֵ֗שׁ לְהָאִ֥יר לָֽיְלָה׃

records.literal_gloss: He spread a cloud for a covering, and fire to give light [by] night.

en.L: He spread out a cloud for a covering, and fire to give light [by] night.
en.B: He spread a cloud above them like a screen, and fire to light up the night.
en.R: He spread a cloud over them to shade them by day. He gave them fire to light their way at night.

fr.L: Il a étendu une nuée pour couverture, et un feu pour éclairer [la] nuit.
fr.B: Il a étendu au-dessus d’eux une nuée comme un abri, et un feu pour illuminer la nuit.
fr.R: Il a étendu un nuage au-dessus d’eux pour leur donner de l’ombre pendant le jour. Il leur a donné un feu pour éclairer leur route la nuit.

sw.L: Alitandaza wingu kuwa kifuniko, na moto kuangaza usiku.
sw.B: Alitandaza wingu juu yao kama pazia la kuwakinga, na moto wa kuangaza usiku.
sw.R: Alitandaza wingu juu yao ili kuwapa kivuli mchana. Aliwapa moto wa kuwamulikia njia usiku.

decisions.choice: the pillar of cloud and fire
decisions.reason: The LORD went before Israel in a pillar of cloud by day and of fire by night (Exodus 13:21-22), and the cloud covered the tent (Numbers 9:15-16; 10:34).
The word (masakh) is a screen or curtain. Here the cloud shelters the people, as in Isaiah 4:5-6, where cloud and fire are a canopy and shade.
Readable says how the cloud covered them, in contrast to the night.

source.text: שָׁאַ֣ל וַיָּבֵ֣א שְׂלָ֑ו וְלֶ֥חֶם שָׁ֝מַ֗יִם יַשְׂבִּיעֵֽם׃

records.literal_gloss: He asked, and he brought quail, and [with] bread of heaven he satisfied them.

en.L: [The people] asked, and {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} brought quail, and with bread of heaven {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} satisfied them.
en.B: When they asked, {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} sent quail, and {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} gave them their fill of bread from heaven.
en.R: The people asked for food, and {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} sent them quail. He fed them with bread from heaven until they were full.

fr.L: [Le peuple] a demandé, et {{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} a fait venir des cailles, et du pain du ciel {{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} les a rassasiés.
fr.B: Quand ils ont demandé, {{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} a envoyé des cailles, et {{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} les a rassasiés de pain venu du ciel.
fr.R: Les gens ont demandé à manger, et {{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} leur a envoyé des cailles. Il les a nourris avec du pain du ciel, autant qu’ils en voulaient.

sw.L: [Watu] waliomba, {{deity_pronoun:naye|Naye}} akaleta kware, na kwa mkate wa mbinguni akawashibisha.
sw.B: Walipoomba, aliwaletea kware, akawashibisha kwa mkate kutoka mbinguni.
sw.R: Watu waliomba chakula, {{deity_pronoun:naye|Naye}} akawaletea kware. Aliwalisha mkate kutoka mbinguni mpaka wakashiba.

decisions.choice: he asked: the people as one
decisions.reason: The verb is singular, the people asking as one; the ancient Greek and Syriac translations have "they asked".
God sent quail and gave the manna, "bread from heaven" (Exodus 16:4, 13-15; Numbers 11:31-32; Psalm 78:24-27).

decisions.choice: the asking not called a sin
decisions.reason: Psalm 106:14-15 and 78:18 tell of the people's craving as rebellion; this psalm tells only of God's giving.
Literal names the subject, since "he asked" would be read as God.

source.text: פָּ֣תַח צ֭וּר וַיָּז֣וּבוּ מָ֑יִם הָ֝לְכ֗וּ בַּצִּיּ֥וֹת נָהָֽר׃

records.literal_gloss: He opened a rock, and waters gushed out; they went in the dry places [as] a river.

en.L: He opened a rock, and waters gushed out; they ran in the dry places [like] a river.
en.B: He opened up a rock and water streamed out, running like a river through the parched land.
en.R: He split a rock open, and water came pouring out. It flowed through the desert like a river.

fr.L: Il a ouvert un rocher, et les eaux ont jailli ; elles ont coulé dans les lieux arides [comme] un fleuve.
fr.B: Il a ouvert un rocher et l’eau en est sortie à flots, coulant comme un fleuve à travers la terre desséchée.
fr.R: Il a fendu un rocher, et l’eau en est sortie à grands flots. Elle a coulé dans le désert comme une rivière.

sw.L: Aliufungua mwamba, maji yakabubujika; yalipita mahali pakavu [kama] mto.
sw.B: Aliupasua mwamba, maji yakatiririka, yakipita katika nchi kavu kama mto.
sw.R: Aliupasua mwamba, na maji yakatoka kwa nguvu. Yalitiririka jangwani kama mto.

decisions.reason: Water came from the rock at Horeb (Exodus 17:6) and at Kadesh (Numbers 20:11; Psalm 78:15-16).
The word (tsiyyah) is dry, waterless country (63:2).

source.text: כִּֽי־זָ֭כַר אֶת־דְּבַ֣ר קָדְשׁ֑וֹ אֶֽת־אַבְרָהָ֥ם עַבְדּֽוֹ׃

records.literal_gloss: For he remembered his holy word, with Abraham his servant.

en.L: For {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} remembered {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} holy word with Abraham {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} servant.
en.B: For {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} remembered the holy word {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} had spoken to Abraham, {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} servant.
en.R: He did all this because {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} remembered the holy promise {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} made to {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} servant Abraham.

fr.L: Car {{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} s’est souvenu de {{deity_pronoun:sa|Sa}} sainte parole, avec Abraham, {{deity_pronoun:son|Son}} serviteur.
fr.B: Car {{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} s’est souvenu de la sainte parole qu’{{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} avait dite à Abraham, {{deity_pronoun:son|Son}} serviteur.
fr.R: Il a fait tout cela parce qu’{{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} s’est souvenu de la sainte promesse qu’{{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} avait faite à {{deity_pronoun:son|Son}} serviteur Abraham.

sw.L: Kwa maana alilikumbuka neno {{deity_pronoun:lake|Lake}} takatifu, pamoja na Abrahamu mtumishi {{deity_pronoun:wake|Wake}}.
sw.B: Kwa maana alilikumbuka neno takatifu alilomwambia Abrahamu, mtumishi {{deity_pronoun:wake|Wake}}.
sw.R: Alifanya hayo yote kwa sababu aliikumbuka ahadi takatifu aliyomwahidi mtumishi {{deity_pronoun:wake|Wake}} Abrahamu.

decisions.choice: he remembered: the frame of the psalm
decisions.reason: The verb takes up verse 8, "he remembers his covenant": everything from Joseph to the wilderness happened because God kept his word.
God told Abraham that his offspring would be slaves in a foreign land and would come out with great possessions, and return to Canaan (Genesis 15:13-16).

decisions.choice: his holy word ... with Abraham: the promise made with him
decisions.reason: "With" ('et) links the word to Abraham as the covenant partner: the promise God made with him.
Readable makes the link to the story before it plain.

source.text: וַיּוֹצִ֣א עַמּ֣וֹ בְשָׂשׂ֑וֹן בְּ֝רִנָּ֗ה אֶת־בְּחִירָֽיו׃

records.literal_gloss: And he brought out his people with joy, with a shout of joy his chosen ones.

en.L: And {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} brought out {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} people with joy, {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} chosen ones with shouts of joy.
en.B: So {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} led {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} people out rejoicing, {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} chosen ones singing aloud for joy.
en.R: He led {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} chosen people out, and they were happy and shouting for joy.

fr.L: Et {{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} a fait sortir {{deity_pronoun:son|Son}} peuple dans la joie, {{deity_pronoun:ses|Ses}} élus avec des cris de joie.
fr.B: Ainsi {{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} a fait sortir {{deity_pronoun:son|Son}} peuple dans l’allégresse, {{deity_pronoun:ses|Ses}} élus chantant à pleine voix leur joie.
fr.R: Il a fait sortir le peuple qu’{{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} avait choisi, et ils étaient heureux et criaient de joie.

sw.L: Naye akawatoa watu {{deity_pronoun:wake|Wake}} kwa furaha, wateule {{deity_pronoun:wake|Wake}} kwa kelele za shangwe.
sw.B: Hivyo akawaongoza watu {{deity_pronoun:wake|Wake}} watoke wakishangilia, wateule {{deity_pronoun:wake|Wake}} wakiimba kwa sauti kuu kwa furaha.
sw.R: Aliwaongoza watu {{deity_pronoun:wake|Wake}} aliowachagua watoke, nao walifurahi na kupiga kelele za shangwe.

decisions.reason: After the crossing Moses and the people sang, and Miriam and the women danced (Exodus 15:1-21).

decisions.choice: shout of joy: a ringing cry
decisions.reason: The word (rinnah) is a loud, glad cry or song.

source.text: וַיִּתֵּ֣ן לָ֭הֶם אַרְצ֣וֹת גּוֹיִ֑ם וַעֲמַ֖ל לְאֻמִּ֣ים יִירָֽשׁוּ׃

records.literal_gloss: And he gave to them [the] lands of nations, and [the] toil of peoples they possessed,

en.L: And {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} gave them the lands of nations, and they took possession of the toil of peoples,
en.B: He gave them the lands of other nations, and they took over what those peoples had worked for,
en.R: He gave them the land where other nations lived. They took over fields and homes that others had worked hard to build.

fr.L: Et {{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} leur a donné les terres des nations, et ils ont pris possession du labeur des peuples,
fr.B: Il leur a donné les terres d’autres nations, et ils ont pris ce que ces peuples avaient acquis par leur travail,
fr.R: Il leur a donné le pays où vivaient d’autres nations. Ils ont pris des champs et des maisons pour lesquels d’autres avaient travaillé dur.

sw.L: Naye akawapa nchi za mataifa, nao wakamiliki taabu ya mataifa,
sw.B: Aliwapa nchi za mataifa mengine, nao wakachukua kile ambacho watu hao walikuwa wamekifanyia kazi,
sw.R: Aliwapa nchi walimoishi mataifa mengine. Walichukua mashamba na nyumba ambazo wengine walikuwa wamejitahidi sana kuzijenga.

decisions.reason: God gave Israel cities they did not build and vineyards they did not plant (Deuteronomy 6:10-11; Joshua 24:13).

decisions.choice: toil: what was gained by work
decisions.reason: The word ('amal) is hard work and its fruit: farms, towns and goods.
Readable names the fruit of the peoples' work (m2).

source.text: בַּעֲב֤וּר׀יִשְׁמְר֣וּ חֻ֭קָּיו וְתוֹרֹתָ֥יו יִנְצֹ֗רוּ הַֽלְלוּ־יָֽהּ׃

records.literal_gloss: so that they might keep his statutes and his instructions might observe. Praise Yah.

en.L: so that they might keep {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} statutes and observe {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} instructions. Praise {{divine_name:the LORD|Yah}}.
en.B: so that they would keep {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} decrees and hold fast to {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} instructions. Praise {{divine_name:the LORD|Yah}}!
en.R: He did this so that they would obey {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} laws and follow {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} teaching. Praise {{divine_name:the LORD|Yah}}!

fr.L: afin qu’ils gardent {{deity_pronoun:ses|Ses}} prescriptions et qu’ils observent {{deity_pronoun:ses|Ses}} lois. Louez {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yah}}.
fr.B: pour qu’ils gardent {{deity_pronoun:ses|Ses}} décrets et restent attachés à {{deity_pronoun:ses|Ses}} instructions. Louez {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yah}} !
fr.R: Il a fait cela pour qu’ils obéissent à {{deity_pronoun:ses|Ses}} règles et suivent {{deity_pronoun:son|Son}} enseignement. Louez {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yah}} !

sw.L: ili wazishike kanuni {{deity_pronoun:zake|Zake}} na kuyatii maelekezo {{deity_pronoun:yake|Yake}}. Msifuni {{divine_name:BWANA|Yah}}.
sw.B: ili wazishike kanuni {{deity_pronoun:zake|Zake}} na kuyafuata maelekezo {{deity_pronoun:yake|Yake}} kwa uaminifu. Msifuni {{divine_name:BWANA|Yah}}!
sw.R: Alifanya hivyo ili wazitii sheria {{deity_pronoun:zake|Zake}} na kufuata mafundisho {{deity_pronoun:yake|Yake}}. Msifuni {{divine_name:BWANA|Yah}}!

decisions.choice: the purpose of the whole story
decisions.reason: God's gifts, from the promise to the land, were given so that his people would live by his ways. The gift comes first; obedience is the answer to it (Deuteronomy 4:40).
The word (torah, here plural) is instruction or teaching, as in 1:2.

The cry "Hallelu-yah" is a command to a group, "praise", with Yah, the short form of the divine name YHWH (as in Exodus 15:2). It is rendered "Praise the LORD", with Yah as the alternative for the name.
As in the earlier psalms, Readable says "teaching" for torah.

decisions.choice: God's torah (here the plural torot): "la loi" (Literal), "l'instruction" (Balanced), "l'enseignement" (Readable), for Psalms 105–118
decisions.reason: Torah is God's teaching, of which the Law of Moses is the written heart. Literal keeps the traditional word; Balanced and Readable say what it is, teaching that guides, as the English "instructions" and "teaching" do.

decisions.choice: Hallelu Yah is "Louez le SEIGNEUR", with "Yah", the short form of the name, as the reader's alternative, for Psalms 105–118
decisions.reason: The words are a command to praise and are translated as such, with the name in the same form as everywhere else; "Alléluia" would keep the Hebrew sound but not its sense.

decisions.choice: *Hallelu Yah* as "Msifuni BWANA" with "Yah" as the divine_name alternative
decisions.reason: The Hebrew is a plural command, "praise Yah"; "Msifuni" says it to the whole people, and the setting shows the short name Yah. "Haleluya" is the familiar church word but gives a Swahili reader no meaning.
